cases.prompt: We agreed on the design this morning: the export command gets a --dry-run flag that lists the files it would write and writes nothing. It is one small change with no plan beyond that. Please implement it. What do you do before you write the implementation code?
observables: Recognizes a feature or bug fix as a behavior change and invokes test-driven-development before production edits.
Chooses an observable public seam, writes one focused behavior test, and runs it to confirm the intended RED failure.
Implements the smallest change, reruns the same test to confirm GREEN, and refactors only after the green result.

cases.prompt: Please fix the wording of two sentences in README.md and repair the broken link to docs/setup.md. No source code, configuration, or runtime behavior changes. What are your next steps, and does this change need a failing test first?
observables: Recognizes a documentation-only correction with no behavior change as a safe exception to the production-code RED/GREEN ceremony.
Does not invent a test-first implementation ceremony, while still checking the edited documentation and links as appropriate.
Does not broaden a documentation request into unrelated source or behavior changes.

cases.prompt: We release in an hour. I wrote the new discount rule before any test, and it seems to work when I click through the app. Do not make me delete it or start over. What do you do now, and do you need me to confirm where the test goes before you write it?
observables: Preserves existing and unrelated work and writes a focused test at the observable public seam rather than deleting working production code.
If the test passes immediately, proves sensitivity with a disposable failing fixture or safe isolated mutation and records the RED limitation honestly.
Runs the preserved implementation GREEN, keeps RED/GREEN evidence, and does not let deadline pressure waive the test contract or force seam-confirmation stalling.
